title: "Visualization"

    df_print: paged

This document serves as the **main exploratory visualization file** for dataset (daily records from 2013 to 2025). The primary goal is to **discover patterns, trends, anomalies, and potential relationships** in the data through various visualization techniques and statistical summaries.

Different plotting methods, smoothing techniques, comparative overlays (especially highlighting Ramadan periods), rolling statistics, trend analysis, extreme event detection, and hypothesis-driven comparisons are used to uncover possible seasonal behaviors, long-term changes, and month-specific phenomena.

All visualizations and summaries are **exploratory** — they aim to reveal insights rather than test formal hypotheses (although some informal hypotheses are discussed).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library("tidyverse")
library("lubridate")

```

## Loading the cleaned dataset
The cleaned dataset is loaded from CSV. This file contains daily weather variables including temperature, humidity, wind speed, heat index, VPD, etc.
```{r echo=TRUE, message=FALSE}
my_data <- readr::read_csv('D:/climetr/climetr_analysis/datasets/birjand_clean_dataset.csv')
```

## Long-term temperature overview (2013–2025)
This line + smooth plot shows the overall temperature behavior across the entire period, helping to visually identify any long-term warming or seasonal patterns.
```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
my_data %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = full_date, y = temp_air_mean_c), 
            linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey60") +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = full_date, y = temp_air_mean_c),
              method = "loess",
              span = 0.4,
              se = FALSE,
              color = "red", 
              linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year", 
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Mean Daily Temperature – Birjand (2013–2025)",
       x = "Year", y = "Temperature (C°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Yearly temperature with Ramadan highlight (selected year)
We repeat the same visualization approach for humidity, wind speed, dew point, daily temperature range, VPD, Heat Index, and Thermal Discomfort Delta — all for a representative year (2024) with a loess smoothing overlay. The Ramadan period is highlighted in red purely for visual reference, allowing easy inspection of seasonal patterns and overall annual behavior across multiple variables.
```{r}
selected_year <- 2024

my_data %>% filter(year == selected_year) %>% ggplot() +
  geom_line(mapping = aes(x=full_date, y=temp_air_mean_c)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(my_data, year == selected_year & is_ramadan == TRUE), mapping = aes(x=full_date, y=temp_air_mean_c), color="red") +
    geom_smooth(aes(x = full_date, y = temp_air_mean_c),
              method = "loess",
              span = 0.4,
              se = FALSE,
              color = "gray50", 
              linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b",
    expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(title = paste("Daily Mean Temperature –", selected_year),
       subtitle = "Red segment = Ramadan period", x = "Month", y = "Temperature (C°)")
```

This plot overlays loess-smoothed daily mean temperature curves for the last five years (2021–2025), allowing direct visual comparison of seasonal patterns and inter-annual differences.
```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
my_colors <- c(
  "2021" = "#1f77b4",
  "2022" = "#ff7f0e",
  "2023" = "#2ca02c",
  "2024" = "#d62728",
  "2025" = "#9467bd"
)

start_year <- 2021
end_year   <- 2025

p <- ggplot() +
  
  lapply(start_year:end_year, function(yr) {
    geom_smooth(
      data = filter(my_data, year == yr),
      aes(x    = day_of_year,
          y    = temp_air_mean_c,
          color = factor(yr, levels = start_year:end_year)),   # ← مهم
      method   = "loess",
      span     = 0.4,
      se       = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.6,
      show.legend = TRUE
    )
  }) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = my_colors,
    name   = "Year",
    labels = as.character(start_year:end_year)
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 366, by = 30),
    limits = c(1, 366),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title    = paste0("Loess Smoothed Daily Mean Temperature (", start_year, "–", end_year, ")"),
    x        = "Day of Year",
    y        = "Temperature (C°)",
    color    = "Year"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position       = c(0.98, 0.98),
    legend.justification  = c("right", "top"),
    legend.background     = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80", linewidth = 0.4),
    legend.title          = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text           = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor.x    = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position   = "plot"
  )

print(p)
```

```{r}
library(broom)      # برای تمیز کردن خروجی مدل
library(trend)      # برای Mann-Kendall (اگر نصب نیست: install.packages("trend"))
library(Kendall) 

# تابع برای تحلیل یک ماه
analyze_trend <- function(df_month) {
  if (nrow(df_month) < 3) return(tibble(month = unique(df_month$month), note = "کمتر از ۳ سال داده"))
  
  model <- lm(mean_heat_index ~ year, data = df_month)
  
  slope     <- coef(model)[2]
  p_value   <- glance(model)$p.value
  r_squared <- glance(model)$r.squared
  years_span <- max(df_month$year) - min(df_month$year) + 1
  change_total <- slope * (years_span - 1)   # تغییر تقریبی کل دوره
  
  mk_test <- MannKendall(df_month$mean_heat_index)
  
  trend_type <- case_when(
    p_value > 0.05 & mk_test$sl > 0.05 ~ "بدون روند معنادار",
    slope > 0 & mk_test$sl <= 0.05     ~ "صعودی معنادار",
    slope < 0 & mk_test$sl <= 0.05     ~ "نزولی معنادار",
    TRUE                               ~ "روند ضعیف یا نوسانی"
  )
  
  tibble(
    month          = unique(df_month$month),
    slope_per_year = round(slope, 4),
    total_change   = round(change_total, 2),
    lm_p           = round(p_value, 4),
    mk_p           = round(mk_test$sl, 4),
    mk_tau         = round(mk_test$tau, 3),
    trend          = trend_type
  )
}

# اجرا
trend_summary <- data %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map_dfr(analyze_trend) %>%
  arrange(month)

print(trend_summary)
```
Statistically significant increasing trends were observed in two months:

July: +0.15 °C per year (total change ≈ +1.81 °C, p ≈ 0.008–0.024)
November: +0.30 °C per year (total change ≈ +3.54 °C, p ≈ 0.010–0.024)

No significant upward or downward trend was detected in the remaining ten months (p > 0.05 in both linear regression and Mann-Kendall tests).
These warming trends — especially the stronger one in November — allow for additional hypotheses to be explored. For example:

The upward temperature trend in July may have influenced urban water consumption patterns (e.g. higher demand for cooling, drinking, and irrigation). Analyzing historical water consumption and reservoir level data for July could help quantify this potential relationship and improve seasonal water planning in Birjand.
The pronounced warming in November raises questions about other possible impacts, such as changes in agricultural water needs, energy demand for heating/cooling, frost risk patterns, or even public health effects related to temperature variability.

However, long-term trends are not necessarily stable; recent years or short-term fluctuations may currently dominate actual water demand and other outcomes. Therefore, any planning or further hypothesis testing should also incorporate the most recent data available.



4. چه ماه های سال بیشترین روزهای به شدت سرد یا به شدت گرم رو داشتند؟

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)   # برای pivot_longer

# فقط روزهای شدید دما (گرم یا سرد)
extreme_temperature_days <- my_data %>% 
  filter(is_extreme_hot == TRUE | is_extreme_cold == TRUE)

result_wide <- extreme_temperature_days %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = month(full_date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(month_name) %>%
  summarise(
    Very_Hot  = sum(is_extreme_hot,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Very_Cold = sum(is_extreme_cold, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month.name)
  )

# 2. تبدیل به long format
result_long <- result_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Very_Hot, Very_Cold),
    names_to = "Temperature_Type",
    values_to = "Count"
  )

# 3. نمودار نهایی – ستون‌ها کاملاً کنار هم بدون فاصله
ggplot(result_long, aes(x = month_name, y = Count, fill = Temperature_Type)) +
  
  geom_col(
    position = "Dodge",  # کنار هم، بدون فاصله اضافی
    width = 0.45,                                                 # عرض هر ستون
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  
  # اضافه کردن عدد بالای هر ستون
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = Count,                           # یا sprintf("%.0f", Count) برای بدون اعشار
      y = Count
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.70),   # هم‌جهت با ستون‌ها
    vjust = -0.4,                              # کمی بالاتر از بالای ستون
    size = 3.4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Very_Hot"  = "#d73027",    # قرمز برای Very Hot
               "Very_Cold" = "#4575b4"),   # آبی برای Very Cold
    name   = "Extreme Type",
    labels = c("Very Hot", "Very Cold")
  ) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Month") +
  
  labs(
    y       = "Number of Days",
    title   = "Number of Extreme Hot and Cold Days by Month",
    subtitle = "Only days with extreme temperatures (no year separation)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

Analysis of daily mean air temperature shows that August had the highest number of extreme days (54 days: 8 very hot + 46 very cold), followed by October (43 days, mostly very cold) and November (40 days, all very cold). Very hot days were most frequent in June (23 days) and March (22 days).
February stands out with 20 extreme days out of ~28–29 days (~69–71% of the month), consisting of 10 very hot and 10 very cold days. Since February largely overlaps with the Persian month of Bahman, the frequent and sharp temperature fluctuations during this period may contribute to higher rates of common colds and respiratory infections in Birjand, as repeated exposure to extreme cold and rapid temperature variability can impair nasal mucociliary clearance and local immune response, increasing susceptibility to viral infections (as supported by studies showing that cold exposure and temperature variability impair nasal mucociliary clearance and local immune response; e.g., Eccles, 2002; Mourtzoukou & Falagas, 2007).

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# اول داده سال به سال آماده کن
yearly_summary <- my_data %>%
  mutate(year = year(full_date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_extreme = sum(is_extreme_hot | is_extreme_cold, na.rm = TRUE),
    ramadan_extreme = sum((is_extreme_hot | is_extreme_cold) & is_ramadan, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(total_extreme, ramadan_extreme),
               names_to = "type",
               values_to = "Count")

# نمودار
ggplot(yearly_summary, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = Count, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.35), width = 0.35) +
  
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = Count,                           # یا sprintf("%.0f", Count) برای بدون اعشار
      y = Count
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.70),   # هم‌جهت با ستون‌ها
    vjust = -0.4,                              # کمی بالاتر از بالای ستون
    size = 3.4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("total_extreme" = "#999999", "ramadan_extreme" = "#d73027"),
                    labels = c("کل سال", "رمضان")) +
  labs(
    x = "سال",
    y = "تعداد روزهای با دمای شدید",
    title = "تعداد روزهای شدید دمایی در رمضان در مقایسه با کل سال",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
